title: TypeScript
subtitle: JavaScript with a type system: catch mistakes before your code runs, describe your data precisely, and work confidently in large code bases.
description: TypeScript is JavaScript with static types. You write ordinary JavaScript plus annotations that describe what your values are; the TypeScript compiler checks every use against those descriptions before the program runs, then removes the annotations and leaves plain JavaScript that runs anywhere JavaScript does. Microsoft released it in 2012, and it has become the usual way to write JavaScript professionally, from web front ends built with React, Angular or Vue to Node.js servers and tools. This course covers why and how the type system works, basic and literal types, interfaces and type aliases, unions and narrowing, functions and overloads, generics, utility, mapped and conditional types, classes, modules and declaration files, the strictness options, and how to bring TypeScript into existing JavaScript projects and frameworks, ending with a complete small project.

It assumes you can already program in JavaScript: take the [JavaScript course](/en/cs/languages/javascript/) in this series first, or come with equivalent experience. That in turn assumes the Start level of [Lumenary CS](/en/cs/) or equivalent: you know what a variable, a loop and a function are.

To run the examples, install [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en/download) and then TypeScript with `npm install --save-dev typescript` in a project folder ([installation options](https://www.typescriptlang.org/download/)). The official [TypeScript Playground](https://www.typescriptlang.org/play/) runs TypeScript in your browser with nothing to install, and shows the JavaScript it produces and the type of anything you point at. Every complete program in these lessons is type-checked by Lumenary's test suite with `tsc --strict` (TypeScript 5.9) and then run with Node 22; the output shown is what it printed. Code that is meant to show a type error is shown separately, with the compiler's actual message.
